FIX ROUND 726b for story #726 (recipes: a shelf spelled through '..' beneath an absent component refuses, the personal install leaves nothing behind, contributing's `recipes list` is hermetic, and a personal install refuses a name the project shelf holds), on branch story-726-shelf-spellings, already checked out in this worktree at 70f5760f.

You are implementing exactly the operator's ruling below and nothing beside it. Decision 0071 (the architectural principles) is ACCEPTED. Build to it.

OPERATOR RULING, 2026-10-18, on PR #737, verbatim: "accept all for 737, option a". It is recorded on #726 as: every ruling #737 asked is accepted (the Climbing, Unmade and Shadowing texts; decision 0083's #726 extension; assumptions (a) and (b); the read surfaces keeping their warnings; a shadowed name refusing after the fetch; the precedence changes). Ask 8 is OPTION (a), HOIST: "`holding_in` resolves the project shelf before its early return, so on the project origin `Climbing`, and `Unread` for an unreadable project shelf, fire with or without a personal shelf placed. This also accepts the observable change against main that the landing named: with no personal shelf, `recipes show x --dir Cargo.toml` prints the `Unread` text instead of "not found". That change matches #697 ruling 2's accepted text: a project shelf that cannot be read refuses on every verb before either recipe is taken."

HISTORY OF THE BRANCH (cut from main 7ed4acc6; your diff is judged against 70f5760f)
- 0fcfcafd and 70f5760f (story run implement-story-726-recipes-a-sh-658b341e): all four of #726's items, decision 0083's #726 extension (proposed), and Onto::unshadowing judging every planned name. Host exact coverage 100%.
- Its landing (landing-pr-for-story-726-recipes-2da42bce) ruled residual LOW, with no new commit. The LOW (decision 0071 ruling 8, with a ruling 9 coverage gap): crates/brokkr-cli/src/recipes/personal.rs:322-325, `holding_in` returns the project shelf BEFORE its `resolving(Origin::Project, &project)?` call when no personal shelf is placed (XDG_CONFIG_HOME and HOME unset or relative). So the project origin's Climbing refusal fires only when a personal shelf is placed. With both variables removed, in a repository holding .brokkr/recipes/x and no sub, `recipes show x --dir .brokkr/recipes/sub/..` exits 1 with `error: recipe 'x' not found under .brokkr/recipes/sub/..; install it with ...`, and `run --recipe x --recipes-dir <root>/.brokkr/recipes/sub/.. --feature f --no-view` likewise. The test harness's Repo::command (tests/brokkr_folder.rs:102) always sets XDG_CONFIG_HOME, so no test reaches that path.
- When you are done, the branch is the above plus ONE new commit of yours. Do not rebase, squash, amend, or merge main (the branch merges clean with main 05e6787c).

DO THIS, proved by binding tests with exact text and removal controls (plant the shape, see the test fail with the stated text, remove the plant):
1. Hoist `resolving(Origin::Project, &project)?` above the `let Some(personal) = personal else` early return in `holding_in`, so it runs whether or not a personal shelf is placed. Change nothing else in the order.
2. Bind it through the binary with XDG_CONFIG_HOME AND HOME removed from the CHILD's environment, using Command::env_remove on the command the harness builds (never a shell prefix). Expect the exact Climbing text, under the binary's uniform `error: ` prefix, on:
   - `recipes show x --dir .brokkr/recipes/sub/..`;
   - `run --recipe x --recipes-dir <root>/.brokkr/recipes/sub/.. --feature f --no-view`;
   - and the Unread case: `recipes show x --dir Cargo.toml`, which on main prints "not found" and now prints the project shelf's Unread text.
   Each asserts the exit status and that nothing was written. Add a unit test in recipes/personal/personal_tests.rs for `holding_in` with `personal: None` on a climbing project shelf.
   Removal control: restore the early return above the hoisted call and see each new test fail with its stated text. Record the control in the commit message.
   Removing HOME from the child leaves it with no host HOME, which keeps it isolated (decision 0065 slice two requires every CLI test that launches a child to be isolated from the host's HOME). The test's temporary folder must still hold everything the child writes.
3. List every OTHER observable refusal the hoist changes against main, for example a dangling-link project shelf on `run --recipe` with no personal shelf. Each must be a Climbing or Unread refusal that #697 ruling 2's text ("a project shelf that cannot be read refuses on every verb before either recipe is taken") already states. If the hoist changes anything that is NOT such a refusal (a success becoming a refusal outside those two, or a changed exit for a readable shelf), STOP and say so in notes: do not narrow, do not work around.
4. Decision 0083's #726 extension, on this branch:
   - Make the clause "on either origin, every verb ruling 2 names" true of HEAD, and say in one sentence that a project shelf that climbs or cannot be read refuses with or without a personal shelf placed.
   - Flip the extension's Status from proposed to accepted, in the form the earlier accepted extensions use: "accepted — operator ruled 2026-10-18 (PR #737)".
   - If the extension lists texts, check the Climbing and Unread texts byte for byte against personal.rs's Display strings.
   Change no other words.

CARRY, do not change (each goes in your notes for the PR):
- The named follow-ups: the double personal-shelf judgement (personal::add's head, and Origin::place via super::add), whose removal needs recipes.rs; and the climbing() expected-text helper once per test layer (jscpd's gate holds and is the authority).

For the implement phase: fix, then run, all clean, from the worktree root: cargo fmt --all -- --check; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings; cargo test -p brokkr-cli --lib --locked -- recipes::; cargo test -p brokkr-cli --test it --locked -- shelf:: recipes:: contributing:: doc_samples:: doc_truth:: init_stacks:: suppressions:: house_prose:: decisions_index::; typos --hidden; quality/ratchet.sh files, clones and api; `cargo crap --path crates/brokkr-cli/src --format json` for every function you add or change (CC 15 or under, 100 lines or under; an existing function at max(15, its quality/crap-baseline.json row)); git diff --check. recipes.rs is at 787 of its 800-line cap: put nothing new there. personal.rs is at 482.

Every review position, panel member or chief, is READ-ONLY: it changes no tracked file and makes no commit, whatever this text asks. It reports each finding. Only the implement phase fixes a finding the review returns.

Commit one signed-off commit (git commit -s), message "recipes: <what changed> (#726)" in the repository's style, ending with the line "Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>". Never push. Run every command in the foreground and wait for it: never background a command or schedule a wakeup, because a headless seat ends when it waits. Do not run scripts/coverage-exact.sh; the controller runs it.

Threat model (operator ruling, 2026-09-26): catch realistic accidental misuse, and fail closed on what cannot be read. A deliberate, exotic evasion is a LOW residual.

HOST FACTS AND PARALLEL WORK
- Main is origin/main as you find it (05e6787c or later). Main lands only through the merge queue. Do not merge or rebase main.
- READ these whole before you start: issue #726 and its comments; decision 0083's #697 addendum and its #726 extension as on this branch; crates/brokkr-cli/src/recipes/personal.rs and personal_tests.rs whole; tests/shelf.rs's personal-shelf and climbing tests; tests/brokkr_folder.rs's Repo::command.
- Host tools as ci.yml pins them. typos, shellcheck and actionlint live in ~/.local/bin; jscpd, cargo-shear and cargo-crap in ~/.cargo/bin.
- Test modules: the exact-coverage gate leaves out only files named tests.rs or *_tests.rs / *-tests.rs. A test submodule named otherwise counts as PRODUCTION.
- Other work runs in parallel. Stay out of it: decision 0065 slice two (the-forge-b9; NEVER message it, or any brokkr-wt-* seat) runs U8a2a on brokkr-runtime engine* and the CLI tests' child-launch helpers (init_stacks.rs, muninn.rs, realms.rs, tests/support/engine.rs); it owns cli_args.rs, doctor.rs and doctor/capabilities.rs. #288 slice J edits brokkr-runtime bundle*. #717 slice 1 (queued) edits agents/, recipes/, init.rs and init_stacks.rs. This round touches only recipes/personal.rs, personal_tests.rs, tests/shelf.rs and decision 0083.

# OpenSpec analyze

Judge duplication, ambiguity, underspecification, house alignment, coverage gaps, and inconsistency across proposal, deltas, design and tasks. Treat the realm house as the constitution. Return each finding with severity and its earliest owning artifact; zero findings is consistent.

instructions.design:
# OpenSpec design

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/design.md`. Record context, goals and non-goals, decisions with alternatives, risks, migration, and open questions. On return, revise the design and dependent artifacts so no finding is merely acknowledged.

# OpenSpec return

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.

Change location: `openspec/changes/{change}`. Archive operation: ["openspec","archive","{change}","--yes"].

# OpenSpec archive

Folding a change is the last task: run the archive operation named above,
which moves the change directory under `openspec/changes/archive/` and
folds its deltas into `openspec/specs/`. Folding also records which change
wrote which capability, so every capability the change touched carries a
`## Provenance` list.

After the archive operation, open each capability's
`openspec/specs/<capability>/spec.md` that the change touched and append
exactly one line under a `## Provenance` heading held at the end of the
file:

`- \`<archived-directory-name>\` — folded <YYYY-MM-DD>`

`<archived-directory-name>` is the directory the archive operation
created under `openspec/changes/archive/`; `<YYYY-MM-DD>` is the day it
was folded. Append only: never rewrite, reorder or remove an existing
provenance line, because standing truth accumulates and is not edited into
a different meaning. The line is a pointer, not a summary — it names the
change and nothing else, and the why stays in the change directory.

house.content:
This realm is a Rust workspace. Production code is Rust under `crates/`; the
Rust-only architecture is recorded by decision 0009. Semantic changes carry a
decision document with status `proposed` because only the operator accepts one.
Intake seats read `README.md` and decisions 0004 and 0005 before framing a
commission, along with the code and history it touches.

The frozen v1 contracts under `contracts/`, the production table at
`policy/phase-machine.json`, and `reference/` (its schemas included) are
read-only.
A contract change lands as a new version file beside the old one, never as an
edit. The evaluator corpus under `fixtures/` is also frozen and is never
regenerated, only versioned.

Tests are part of every change. Extend the suite that proves the code, run
`cargo test --workspace`, compile `recipes/self`, and leave formatting, clippy,
and the exact-coverage gate clean before reporting success.

Commit completed work with `git` using the repository's message style. Never
push.

The supported hosts are Linux and macOS (decision 0063); WSL2 is Linux. Write
no Windows-conditional code, test or evidence.

## Architecture

Decision 0071 rules how code here is shaped. Build to it, and cite its ruling
numbers in what you judge. Where a gate named below holds a rule, the gate is
the authority, and a finding it would catch is the gate's.

- **Pure core (ruling 1).** `brokkr-core` and `brokkr-view` do no I/O and read
  no clock, environment or randomness. They run no process. Pass `now`, paths
  and environment in as arguments. Effects live in the crates above core and
  view, and are journaled.
- **Enums and data, not traits (ruling 2).** A closed set is an enum matched
  exhaustively, with no wildcard arm that decides behaviour. Anything an
  operator extends is data under `adapters/`, `agents/`, `recipes/` or
  `realms.json`, validated and digested. Add a trait only for a seam whose
  contract spans several operations that must stay consistent with one
  another, reached across a process or service boundary, and name that seam
  in its doc comment. `ProducerTransport` is the one such trait today. A test
  double alone does not make a seam: a single substitutable function is a
  closure seam (`*_with`, `*_in`), which is how the house inverts a
  dependency otherwise.
- **Typed at the edge (ruling 3).** Parse wire, file and harness data once
  into a type, with `serde` and `deny_unknown_fields` where the contract is
  closed. `serde_json::Value` never goes past the edge, into state, or back
  out by string key. Never put `format!("{:?}")` in anything digested or
  journaled. A doubly-optional field or a string vocabulary is a missing enum.
- **Small functions (ruling 4).** New and changed functions stay within 100
  lines, nesting depth 5 and 7 parameters. Cyclomatic complexity follows
  the operator's 2026-09-26 ruling: a function may reach the higher of 15
  and its baseline, so a new function stays within 15, an existing one may
  change freely up to 15, and one already over 15 may only shrink.
  Production files stay within 800 lines and test files within 2,000, and a
  file already over may not grow. Add no new `jscpd` clone in production
  code, test code or data. `quality/` holds the measured baseline. Today's
  offenders carry `#[allow(clippy::…)]`, and #337 converts them to
  `#[expect(clippy::…, reason = "…")]`. Add a suppression only by a ruling,
  and remove it when you fix the function. A new suppression is
  `#[expect(…, reason)]`, never `#[allow]`.
- **Once (ruling 5).** Every fact has one home. A repeated vocabulary, skeleton
  or helper becomes one function or one table. An agent is defined once under
  `agents/`, and seats hire it by reference. A recipe that differs from another
  by a model, a seat or an entry is an `extends` overlay, never a copy. The
  agent library does not yet accept `extends`, and #360 builds it. Until then,
  a variation of an agent lives at the seat that hires it, overridden in a
  recipe overlay. It is never a second agent file that restates the first. A
  copy that must exist, such as a script a bundle pins, is held to its source
  by a test.
- **Nothing unused (ruling 6).** Add no alias, agent, contract version, flag or
  `pub` item without a consumer, and prefer `pub(crate)`. A deprecation names
  the release that removes it.
- **One derivation (ruling 7).** A fact shown on two surfaces is derived once
  in `brokkr-view`. The CLI, the TUI and `ui.html` only paint it. The engine
  never admits anything by a display-crate function.
- **Typed errors (ruling 8).** Return a `thiserror` enum whose `Display` keeps
  the operator's text. Tests match variants and pin each module's text once.
  Add no new `Result<_, String>`.
- **Tests that bind (ruling 9).** Assert exact values or variants, never
  `is_err()` alone. Show that every new test binds: a compiling mutation that
  removes the behaviour must make it fail. Restore the behaviour and record
  the failing test. Share fixtures through builders. Never change the process
  environment without a guard that restores it on unwind. A production guard
  left out because the exact-coverage gate would count it unreachable carries
  a removal-control test for the invariant that makes it unreachable, and the
  comment explaining the omission names that test.
- **The house's patterns (ruling 10).**
  - A harness is a module behind `AdapterKind`. This is the target form;
    today all five kinds share one module, and #347 and #348 build the
    split.
  - A CLI verb is a `Cmd` variant plus a handler.
  - A long parameter list becomes a parameter object.
  - Argv and mount tables are built with a builder.
  - Observing the world is split from deciding on it.
  - Never use a trait-object registry for a closed set.

Judges rate a finding against these rulings by this table, and cite the ruling
number:

- **info:** something a house gate would catch. The gate's verdict is the
  authority.
- **low:** a new or changed function over a ceiling, a rule written a second
  time, an item added without a consumer, or a `Value` carried past its edge
  within one module.
- **medium:** an untyped vocabulary that crosses crates, recipe or agent data
  copied instead of extended, a fact derived a second time on another surface,
  an error matched by its text, or a new test that cannot fail.
- **high or above:** any violation that hides a fail-open path or weakens a
  refusal. It is carried as a security finding.

A principle the implementer bent knowingly, and named with its reason in
`notes`, is still rated, and the judge carries that reason with the finding.

## Release configuration

The release manager prepares the candidate and profile patches; the operator
publishes them. Local validation is preparation work. Remote CI on the final PR
head, publication, channel updates and live-profile verification are handoff
steps, recorded as pending until their remote results exist. Historical
"live from" channel versions and old journal examples are historical facts,
not current-version references to replace.


result.notes:
Implemented the operator's 2026-10-18 ruling on PR #737 (option a, hoist) as one signed (G), signed-off commit aab6ffdc on story-726-shelf-spellings over 70f5760f. Not pushed, rebased or merged.

1. HOIST: in crates/brokkr-cli/src/recipes/personal.rs, holding_in now calls resolving(Origin::Project, &project)? before the `let Some(personal) = personal else` early return. Nothing else moved; the diff is 2 lines.

2. TESTS (both bind):
- tests/shelf.rs shelf::a_project_shelf_refuses_with_no_personal_shelf_placed. It removes XDG_CONFIG_HOME and HOME from the child with Command::env_remove, through the existing `under` helper over Repo::command. It covers three cases: `recipes show x --dir .brokkr/recipes/sub/..` gives the exact Climbing text (shelf as typed, at .brokkr/recipes); `run --recipe x --feature f --no-view --recipes-dir <root>/.brokkr/recipes/sub/..` gives Climbing with absolute paths; `recipes show x --dir Cargo.toml` gives the exact Unread text ('Cargo.toml: not a directory'). Every message carries the `error: ` prefix. Each case asserts exit 1, repo.files() byte for byte, the fake driver's state count, and finally the runs and queue ledger.
- personal_tests.rs a_climbing_project_shelf_refuses_with_no_personal_shelf: holding_in("x", <project>/sub/.., None) returns Unshelved::Climbing{Project, shelf, at=<project>} with the exact text.
REMOVAL CONTROL (run, recorded in the commit message): with the early return restored above the call, the unit test panicked at personal_tests.rs:343 (unwrap_err on Ok("/tmp/.../project/sub/..")). The shelf test failed at its first case with left (Some(1), "error: recipe 'x' not found under .brokkr/recipes/sub/..; install it with `brokkr recipes add <source> --name x`"). With the assertion made non-fatal for the control only, the run case and the Cargo.toml case each printed the same 'not found under <shelf>' text in place of Climbing or Unread. The assertion and the order were restored, and both tests pass.

3. OTHER OBSERVABLE CHANGES vs the pre-hoist order, with no personal shelf placed. I ran a temporary survey test under both orders, then deleted it (outputs in .forge/survey-old.txt and .forge/survey-new.txt). A project shelf that is a dangling link, a file, or a looping link now refuses `recipes show`, `run`, `resume`, `rerun` and `queue add` of `x` with the Unread text (causes ENOENT os error 2, 'not a directory', ELOOP os error 40). Before, the first four printed "recipe 'x' not found" (exit 1). `queue add` exited 0 ('queued entry N'), so it is a success that becomes a refusal. It is an Unread refusal on a verb #697 ruling 2 names ('refuses on every verb before either recipe is taken'), so it is inside the ruling and I did not stop. By code reading, not observed: an ancestor whose metadata cannot be read (EACCES) or a path through a file (ENOTDIR) also becomes Unread. Unchanged, observed under both orders: a readable shelf (all five verbs exit 0), an absent shelf ('not found', exit 1), and `..` beneath a standing `sub` (run starts). Nothing outside Climbing and Unread changed, so the STOP condition was not met.

4. DECISION 0083, #726 extension: Status now reads 'accepted — operator ruled 2026-10-18 (PR #737)'. After '...naming the shelf as spelled and that entry.' I added one sentence: 'A project shelf that climbs or cannot be read refuses with or without a personal shelf placed.' The next line was rewrapped with no words changed. Byte-for-byte checks: `grep -cxF` found the Climbing line (in the extension) and the Unread line (ruling 2's text) once each, using the Display templates with placeholders.
